manifest.purpose: Hardened HLS-compatible implementation of `uint32_t modexp(uint32_t base, uint32_t exponent, uint32_t modulus)`. Uses fixed 32-iteration left-to-right square-and-multiply-always with constant-time select (bit mask, no branch) to conditionally apply the multiply result: computes square every iteration, computes multiply-candidate every iteration via a multiply-stub hook (weak symbol / function pointer named `modexp_multiply_hook` compiled in as plain multiply by default, replaceable by counting-stub at link time for SR1 test), and selects between candidate and previous accumulator using arithmetic mask on the current exponent bit (no if/branch on secret data). Exposes a static/global iteration counter via a designated hook function `uint32_t modexp_get_last_iterations()` incremented exactly 32 times per call, used by FR4/SR2 harness. No printf/exit/dynamic allocation; no STL; only fixed-size scalars. Handles base=0, exponent=0, modulus edge cases per FR2 (mod-reduces base first, accumulator starts at 1 mod modulus, all reductions unconditional). No exponent-derived global state beyond the fixed iteration counter (which is exponent-value-independent, always 32).

Reference INSECURE baseline (classic branchy square-and-multiply): loop over 32 bits, square every iteration, but only multiply when exponent bit is 1 guarded by an `if` branch, so the multiply-stub invocation count varies with exponent Hamming weight. Same public function signature and same iteration-counter hook (fixed 32) so FR1-FR3 still pass, but SR1 (multiply count varies, not constant 32) and SR2 (multiply-schedule trace varies with exponent) fail. Used only to demonstrate the harness discriminates correctly per acceptance criteria; not used as the golden submission artifact itself (golden/modexp_kernel.cpp is the one staged over inputs/modexp_kernel.cpp for grading).
